claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 begins in a high-temperature disordered BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is primarily governed by the degree of Al-induced chemical ordering.
Al-induced chemical ordering destabilizes the high-temperature disordered BCC phase.
An ordered state such as B2 or another ordered derivative becomes thermodynamically favored once kinetic hindrances are overcome.
Al-mediated chemical ordering creates local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions modify the alloy's free-energy landscape.
Increasing Al content promotes local lattice distortion.
Al-associated lattice distortion encourages ordered-phase formation by reducing the free-energy difference between disordered BCC and the ordered phase.
Slow cooling or extended annealing provides sufficient atomic mobility for ordering to proceed.
Slow-cooled or prolonged-annealed samples will have greater long-range chemical order than rapidly quenched samples.
Slow cooling or prolonged annealing will transform disordered BCC into an ordered phase.
Rapid quenching kinetically traps the high-temperature disordered BCC phase by preventing significant atomic rearrangement.
The proposed mechanism is specific to Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 and its thermal-processing window.
Additional alloying elements or substantially different processing routes may alter the relevant kinetics or thermodynamic landscape.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the disordered BCC phase is destabilized by lowering its free energy relative to the ordered state, but lowering the BCC free energy relative to the ordered state would instead stabilize BCC. Elsewhere, the mechanism states that the ordered phase is thermodynamically favored.
